raw_response:
Well, I've been farming these 10.7 mu for 30 years now, and at 65 my legs aren't what they used to be, but I still know every patch of this land. My son works in the factory in Handan, so it's mostly me, my wife, and my daughter-in-law at home with the two grandchildren. We need the wheat for our own flour and the maize to sell for cash, plus some for the pigs.

**Winter wheat — all 10.7 mu**

I'm planting wheat in the first week of October, same as always. Last year I got about 420 jin per mu, which was decent — not great, not bad. My neighbor Lao Zhang tried some new fancy seed and didn't do much better, so I'm sticking with the improved Jinmai variety I've been using. Costs me about 55 yuan per mu for seed.

For fertilizer, I usually put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — that's about 50 kg. The shop says it's 15-15-15 or something like that, but I just know one bag. Then at jointing, around Qingming, if the wheat looks a bit yellow I'll spread another half bag of urea, maybe 20-25 kg. That should be enough. I don't want to skimp — last year my cousin cut back and his yield dropped badly. Better to put a little more than too little. So total nitrogen is probably around 15-16 kg per mu, I suppose.

Irrigation — I'll water three times. Once right after planting if it doesn't rain, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. The well water isn't free anymore, they meter it now, so I watch it. But three times is what everyone does, and I've done it for years.

For pesticide, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring when the weeds come up. If I see aphids later, maybe insecticide. That's usually enough.

Tillage — I'll plow once after the maize comes off, then harrow it smooth before wheat planting. I hire Old Wang's tractor for plowing, costs me but saves my back.

Labor — my wife and I do most of it. Planting takes us about 3 days, spreading fertilizer another 2 days, irrigation we manage together about 4 days total. Harvesting wheat, I usually hire the combine, takes half a day but costs money. I'll say 12 family days and 2 hired days for the harvest help.

Yield — I'm hoping for about 430 kg per mu. The soil is alright, not the best in the village but not the worst either.

**Summer maize — all 10.7 mu**

Maize goes in right after wheat comes off, mid-June. Last year we had rain right after planting, which was good. The window is tight — sometimes only 3-4 days between harvest and planting. I'll hire the tractor to plow quick, then plant.

Seed — hybrid maize, Zhengdan 958 or something similar from the seed shop. About 60 yuan per mu. Can't save seed from hybrids, so I buy fresh every year.

Fertilizer — I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 45 kg per mu. Then if the rains are good I might not need more, but usually I topdress with urea at the big trumpet leaf stage, about 20 kg per mu. So nitrogen around 14-15 kg per mu total.

Irrigation — twice for maize. Once if it's dry at planting, and once at flowering if there's no rain. Sometimes once is enough if the summer rains come. I'll plan for two times to be safe.

Pesticide — herbicide at planting, that's the main thing. Maybe insecticide if the corn borer shows up.

Tillage — quick rotary till after wheat harvest, then plant. No time for deep plowing.

Labor — planting is rushed, 2 family days plus I might hire 1 day of help. Managing it through summer is easier, about 8 family days total. Harvest in late September, the combine does most of it. Say 10 family days and 2 hired days.

Yield — expecting about 480 kg per mu. Last year was close to 500, but you can't count on that.

**Money**

Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation water, hired labor — all together I'm looking at about 7,800 yuan for inputs this year. That's a lot for us. I have about 9,000 yuan put aside for farming, so I'll have a little left for emergencies. I thought about adding more fertilizer, but my daughter-in-law says we should keep 1,000 yuan in reserve in case the well pump breaks again. She's right.
